bug_semantics: In ALSA USB-audio implicit-feedback playback, snd_usb_handle_sync_urb() (sound/usb/endpoint.c) converts each inbound isochronous packet's actual_length into a playback frame count by dividing by the sync-source (sender) stride and writes that value straight into out_packet->packet_size[i] with no min() against ep->maxframesize. A connected USB audio device fully controls those IN packet lengths. Because playback then multiplies the stored frame count by the (often larger) playback stride, an oversized capture packet becomes an even larger outbound packet. The unclamped sizes are enqueued and memcpy'd into ctx->packet_size by snd_usb_queue_pending_output_urbs(), then consumed by prepare_playback_urb() (sound/usb/pcm.c) and prepare_silent_urb() to set urb->iso_frame_desc[].length and to memset/copy into the URB DMA buffer allocated as maxsize * packets. Before the Feb 2026 consumer-side cap, that produced URB submissions past the endpoint's hardware frame/packet limit and out-of-bounds writes into kernel-coherent USB buffers (C/I/A high via local USB gadget). The 2026-07-28 fix clamps the computed frame count at the store site in snd_usb_handle_sync_urb().
flaw_origin: The vulnerable sender-stride conversion was first written in 28acb12014fb0c3e1edfdab1b1e3e266cf651550 (2012-11-28, Eldad Zack, committed by Takashi Iwai): a 9-line change in sound/usb/endpoint.c that replaced actual_length / ep->stride with actual_length / sender->stride so implicit-feedback packet sizes would match when capture and playback channel counts differ (M-Audio Fast Track C400). The assignment remained unclamped. Immediate parent fde854bdaf603a99a80b9545c0aaca9ccd02dd31 still divided by ep->stride and contains no sender->stride. git log -L shows only one earlier writer of the loop, 8fdff6a319e7dac757c558bd283dc4577e68cde7 (v3.5, ep->stride, no clamp); the Linux CNA marks versions before 3.8 unaffected, so that precursor is not this CVE's BIC. 28acb120 is a single-parent mainline patch, not a move, revert, backport, or squash.

reasoning: CVE-2026-74497 is a published Linux CNA record, not withdrawn or rejected. The sink is the implicit-feedback path in snd_usb_handle_sync_urb() storing an unclamped sender-stride frame count into the playback packet queue, which historically drove iso URB lengths past ep->maxframesize and the allocated DMA buffer. Line history and the CNA/Fixes tag converge on 28acb12014fb0c3e1edfdab1b1e3e266cf651550 as the smallest commit that first wrote those vulnerable lines (sender->stride assignment). The immediate parent still uses ep->stride, so the mechanism is absent there. 8fdff6a introduced an earlier unclamped ep->stride variant in v3.5, but the CNA explicitly leaves pre-3.8 unaffected and the advisory names sender-stride scaling; 8fdff6a is therefore a precursor, not this CVE's BIC. 28acb120 is a 2012 single-parent human patch (Eldad Zack / Takashi Iwai) with only Signed-off-by trailers and no commit-object AI marker. The 2026 fix's Assisted-by: Jetski:Gemini-3.6-Flash is AI-on-fix and does not change BIC authorship. Verdict is NOT_AI.
